That is consistent across dev and holdout and is too large to be fit noise, so the selection rule is the suspect, not the features. Lead hypothesis (from c7e3-02): decide_av fires at the FIRST bar whose predicted value clears the cut (optional stopping, early fires), while the control is uniform. Post-reset iteration 3, authored from this diagnosis: (a) measure the fire-bar k / bars-held distribution, policy vs control, from the shard outputs; (b) a pre-registered unit that keeps the value models but changes the selection to a uniform-timing-matched decision (score once at a fixed decision bar, or fire only where the predicted value is the trade's running maximum over a fixed lookback), still against the same random control. Second structural lead: random tighten/bank beats HOLD by ~+0.06 R/trade net; a pre-registered non-ML 'random-bar tighten' arm is effectively a time-stop or giveback rule and is worth stating as its own unit (it needs no model). Data: all 24 policy shards of a9d2-02 (av_tighten, run 45581671996), 108,922 fired dev trades (entry < 2026-01-01). Script: scratchpad os_measure.py, to be committed with the iteration-3 PR. (1) WHEN it fires: 87.1% of fires are at the FIRST decision bar (k=1); k p25/p50/p75 = 1/1/1. Fire point as a share of the HOLD path length: p50 0.056. (2) What that costs: fires at k/bars_held < 0.1 (65% of fires) give policy-HOLD -16,376 R (-0.23 R/trade). On those same trades, the uniform control gives +2,492 R. HOLD win rate there is 0.39, so these are mostly the eventual winners, cut early. Where the policy fires later (k/held 0.1-0.5, 33% of fires), policy and control are equal (+0.40 vs +0.41 R/trade). The model's choice of bar adds nothing over random once it is not early. (3) By bar: at k=1, policy -0.014 R/trade vs control +0.172 R/trade on the same 94,914 trades. CONCLUSION: the value model's predicted value is highest at the first bar for most trades, and the first-crossing rule acts on it there. The structural gain is tightening AFTER the trade has developed, which uniform placement captures.
